title: Microsoft Teams: users can report a security concern in meetings
summary: The reporting controls, default state and rollout dates are supported. The licensing field incorrectly says licensing is not yet published: Microsoft explicitly includes reporting of meetings and meeting participants in Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 and Plan 2.

claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: Report a Security Concern in Meetings

claims.quote:
The Microsoft Teams app for iOS/iPadOS: Version 7.15 or later (messages only).
The Microsoft Teams app for Android: Version 1416/1.0.0.2025153104 or later (messages only).

claims.claim: The meeting page directs admins to the policy or settings page controlling reporting for Teams meetings and then Allow users to report meetings, without a concrete navigation page name.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, open the policy or settings page that controls reporting for Teams meetings.
Select the Allow users to report meetings policy.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global supports -ReportMeeting with Enabled or Disabled to control tenant meeting reporting.
claims.quote:
The only valid input is Global

Controls whether end users can access the "Report a concern" and "Report as not a concern" options in the meeting experience (including meeting UI and meeting chat).

Possible values:
- Enabled
- Disabled

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify ReportMeeting as the setting behind the Teams admin centre toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow users to report meetings" "ReportMeeting". Opened end-user-reporting-teams-meeting, submissions-teams and Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration; the pages describe each control without explicitly mapping them.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Global Administrator or Teams Administrator can view or configure Teams reporting settings.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in the Teams admin center, you need to be a member of the Global Administrator or Teams Administrator roles.

claims.claim: Destination settings are in Defender portal > Settings > Email & collaboration > Teams user reported settings tab > Reported item destinations > Send the reported items to.
claims.quote:
go to Settings > Email & collaboration > Teams user reported settings tab.

settings in the Reported item destinations section on the Teams user reported settings page

Send the reported items to

claims.claim: The documented Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy call with ReportChatMessageEnabled true, ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled true and ReportChatMessageAddresses sends to Microsoft and the specified mailbox.
claims.quote:
Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy -Identity DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy `
    -ReportChatMessageEnabled $true `
    -ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled $true `
    -ReportChatMessageAddresses "securityadmin@contoso.com"

claims.claim: The destination configuration commands use Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in Teams by using PowerShell, connect to Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Teams user reported destination settings also govern reported meetings and participants despite the chat-named parameters.
claims.quote: When users report Teams messages or calls or report meetings or meeting participants as malicious or non malicious, the reported items are sent to Microsoft and/or the reporting mailbox as defined by the Teams user reported settings in Defender for Office 365.

claims.claim: The Microsoft-only destination call uses ReportChatMessageEnabled true, ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled false and EnableUserEmailNotification true.
claims.quote:
Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy -Identity DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy `
    -ReportChatMessageEnabled $true `
    -ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled $false `
    -EnableUserEmailNotification $true

claims.claim: Monitoring is at Defender portal > Settings > Email & collaboration > Teams user reported settings tab > Microsoft Teams > Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote:
go to Settings > Email & collaboration > Teams user reported settings tab.

On the Teams user reported settings page, go to the Microsoft Teams section for the Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams setting.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Organization Management or Security Administrator can modify the Defender monitoring setting.
claims.quote: To modify the Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams setting in the Defender portal, you need to be a member of the Organization Management or Security Administrator role groups.

claims.claim: Defender monitoring is enabled by default for new tenants.
claims.quote: The Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams setting is turned on by default for new tenants; existing tenants need to enable it.

claims.claim: Existing tenants need to enable Defender monitoring for reported items to show correctly on User reported.
claims.quote: Existing tenants need to enable it. If user reporting of messages, calls, or meetings is turned on in the Teams admin center, it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported items to show up correctly on the User reported tab on the Submissions page.

claims.claim: The Defender monitoring setting is meaningful only when the corresponding Teams reporting capability is enabled.
claims.quote: When the applicable setting is turned off, users can't report those items within Teams, so the corresponding setting in the Microsoft Defender portal is irrelevant.

claims.claim: No separate API or command is documented for the Defender monitoring toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: "Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams" PowerShell ReportSubmissionPolicy; "Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams" "API". Opened submissions-teams and Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy; documented parameters specify destinations, not this toggle.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance guidance; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: Administrators can review reported meeting details at Defender portal > Submissions > User reported.
claims.quote:
SecOps team members can review submitted Teams message, call, meeting, or meeting participant details in the following locations in the Defender portal:

The User reported tab of the Submissions page

claims.claim: The notice ties detailed meeting submissions in Defender to Defender for Office 365 Plan 1, Plan 2 or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: Organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1, Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR will be able to review detailed reported meeting submissions in the Microsoft Defender portal.

claims.claim: Reported meeting details are also accessible through View submission in the Defender XDR incident.
claims.quote:
SecOps team members can review submitted Teams message, call, meeting, or meeting participant details in the following locations in the Defender portal:

The View submission action in the Defender XDR incident.

claims.claim: No API for reviewing user-reported meeting submissions is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reported meetings submissions Microsoft Graph API user reported security submissions report export API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph Teams meeting security reports submissions threatSubmission. Opened SecOps guide and Graph beta threatSubmission: no meeting submission type.

claims.claim: Alert policies are at Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Alert policy.
claims.quote: To view and create alert policies, in the Microsoft Defender portal, under Email & collaboration select Policies & rules > Alert policy.

claims.claim: Reported meetings and participants generate the same alert policies as reported calls.
claims.quote: Reported meetings and meeting participants generate the same alert policies as reported calls.

claims.claim: The user-report alerts do not currently generate AIR investigations.
claims.quote: Currently, these alerts don't generate automated investigation and response (AIR) investigations.

claims.claim: Manage Alerts is required to create and edit alert policies.
claims.quote: You have to be assigned the Manage Alerts role to create and edit alert policies.

claims.claim: Built-in alert policies allow toggling, notification recipients and daily notification limits, but not editing other settings.
claims.quote: You can turn off these policies (or back on again), set up a list of recipients to send email notifications to, and set a daily notification limit. The other settings for these policies can't be edited.

claims.claim: No supported command for changing these built-in alert policies is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: built-in alert policies Teams call reported Set-ProtectionAlert PowerShell. Opened alert-policies; read Set-ProtectionAlert reference search excerpt: "You can't use this cmdlet to edit default alert policies." No applicable alternative found.

claims.claim: The Teams report is at Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports tab > User reported security submissions.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports.
On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent for the Teams user-reported security submissions report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "User reported security submissions" PowerShell API Teams; Teams reported meetings submissions Microsoft Graph API user reported security submissions report export API. Opened end-user-reported-security-signal: UI and CSV export, no automation endpoint.

claims.claim: The Teams report documentation lists Calling, Chats and channels, and User, but not a meetings category.
claims.quote: Searched: "User reported security submissions" PowerShell API Teams. Read end-user-reported-security-signal in full: Report category lists Calling, Chats and channels, User; no meetings category.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Scope; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: User reporting requires an online Teams mailbox and does not support on-premises user mailboxes.
claims.quote:
User reporting in Teams is supported only for users with an online Teams mailbox.

On-premises mailboxes aren't supported in either scenario.

claims.claim: The reporting mailbox must be in Exchange Online, not on-premises.
claims.quote: The reporting mailbox configured in Teams user reported settings must also be an Exchange Online mailbox. On-premises mailboxes aren't supported in either scenario.

claims.claim: Learn says Teams reporting of calls, meetings and messages is unsupported in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: User reporting of calls, meetings, and messages in Teams is not supported in U.S. Government organizations (Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC High, and DoD).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Sending reports to Microsoft copies meeting and participant metadata into ongoing algorithm reviews.
claims.quote:
When a user reports a Teams item to Microsoft, the following data associated with the item is copied and included in ongoing algorithm reviews, as applicable:

Meeting metadata.
Meeting participant metadata.

claims.claim: Microsoft personnel might review submitted meeting and participant metadata, which is typically not permitted for Teams items.
claims.quote: Microsoft personnel might read submitted messages and files and review submitted call, meeting, and participant metadata, which is typically not permitted for Teams items in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Submitted content is stored in data centres in the USA.
claims.quote: Submitted content is stored in secured, compliance-audited data centers located in the USA and is deleted as soon as it's no longer required.

claims.claim: The destination options are Microsoft and my reporting mailbox, Microsoft only, and My reporting mailbox only; Microsoft cites the first as its default.
claims.quote:
Send the reported items to > Microsoft only
Send the reported items to > My reporting mailbox only

That's why we use Send the reported items to > Microsoft and my reporting mailbox as the default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: My reporting mailbox only prevents submission to Microsoft unless an administrator submits the item manually from User reported.
claims.quote: If you select Send the reported items to > My reporting mailbox only, reported items don't go to Microsoft for analysis unless an admin manually submits the item from the User reported tab on the Submissions page

claims.claim: Reported items remain visible to users.
claims.quote: Reported items remain visible to users.

claims.claim: Users can report the same item multiple times.
claims.quote: Users can report the same items multiple times.

claims.claim: Microsoft's reporting pages do not describe an automatic action against a reported meeting participant.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting reported participant automatic removal blocking report security concern. Opened meeting reporting, submissions-teams, SecOps guide and Teams protection overview; reporting is an investigation signal, with no automatic participant action described.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft documents meeting reporting in organisations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report messages, calls, meetings, or meeting participants in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown, meaning Microsoft has not yet published it.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 provides the following extra Teams protection features:

Report Teams items: Users can report Teams messages, calls, meetings, or meeting participants as malicious or not malicious.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included". Start licensing.notes with "Meeting and participant reporting is included in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 and Plan 2." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/mdo-support-teams-about, whose feature table lists user-reported meetings and participants in both plans. Retain the separately qualified uncertainty about Teams admin center access without Defender.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a licence specifically for viewing meeting reports in the Teams admin center without Defender.
